articles.title: Oljepriset sjunker något när handeln öppnat
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Oljepriset sjunker något när handeln öppnat
articles.body_text: Svart rök stiger från en attackerat oljeanläggning i Riyad. Bild från helgen. Oljepriset sjunker något när handeln öppnat Oljepriset sjunker något efter att den internationella handelns öppning vid 23-tiden svensk tid. När handeln hade varit öppen i cirka 20 minuter hade terminspriset på Nordsjöolja (Brent) fallit till 115,27 dollar per fat. Amerikansk WTI-olja hade sjunkit till 101,71 dollar per fat. I förra veckan steg oljan ordentligt och när handeln stängde i fredags låg Brent på 116,72 dollar, WTI-oljan kostade 103,27 dollar. I helgen har den Iranstödda Huthirörelsen i Jemen genomfört en lång rad nya drönar- och robotattacker mot Saudiarabiens flygplatser och oljeindustri. Saudiarabien har i sin tur satt in flyganfall mot mål i Jemen. Innan USA och Israel inledde kriget mot Iran den 28 februari kostade oljan cirka 70 dollar.

articles.title: Kina viker – europeiska lyxjättar dyker
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Kina viker – europeiska lyxjättar dyker
articles.body_text: Lyxkonglomeratet LVMH:s vd Bernard Arnault är 76 år och har signalerat att han är redo att leda koncernen i tio år till. Arkivbild. Efter tio års köpfest viker plötsligt efterfrågan i Kina. Det gör att börsvärdet för sex europeiska börsjättar har rasat med motsvarande 2 800 miljarder kronor i år. När tillväxten viker, driven av en köpstark kinesisk medelklass, har branschens motor börjat hacka. Europas sex största börsnoterade lyxbolag – LVMH, Kering, Hermès, Richemont, Prada och Moncler – har i år tappat 251 miljarder euro (motsvarande cirka 2 800 miljarder kronor) i börsvärde, rapporterar Dagens industri med Financial Times (FT) som källa. Värst har LVMH och Hermès drabbats, som också är de två största aktörerna. Enligt FT är beror det på att en lång svacka på Kinas fastighetsmarknad och på att landets svaga börsutveckling har urholkat köpkraften.

articles.title: Klomaskin – nytt grepp för inflationstrött japan
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Klomaskin – nytt grepp för inflationstrött japan
articles.body_text: En kvinna satsar för att vinna toalettpapper i en klomaskin. Klomaskin – nytt grepp för inflationstrött japan I normala fall är högsta vinsten ett gosedjur eller någon annan leksak. Nu lockas spelarna av ett paket ägg eller toalettpapper. Japans spelautomater har fått ett helt nytt innehåll när landets hushåll tyngs under inflationstrycket. Nyhetsbyrån AFP har intervjuat en rad japaner, som exempelvis Minae Kamata, kring det nya fenomenet. Den 25-åriga hemmafrun styr med van hand den klo som är tänkt att fiska upp några av de priser som ligger inuti spelmaskinen. Den här gången handlar det dock om att försöka få upp just ett paket med toalettpapper. Om du har lite tur så blir det samma pris som att köpa på rabatt, säger hon efter att ha lyckats på andra försöket. Insatsen för ett försök är 100 japanska yen, motsvarande cirka sex svenska kronor. I vanliga fall handlar det om ett traditionellt nöje eller hobby för japaner som totalt sett omsätter flera miljarder kronor årligen, nu har man dock börjat förena nöje med nytta. I Japan ligger inflationen på omkring 2 procent, i ett globalt perspektiv fortfarande väldigt lågt, men för många japanska hushåll är det betydligt svettigare än man är vana vid. Detta gör nu att spelmaskinerna fylls med ägg, ris och tvättmedel för att locka till spel. En familj kan göra av med 10 000 yen på en dag med karaoke eller bowling och ha roligt men det är också allt. Här kan du gå hem med toalettpapper, flaskor eller leksaker, säger Teruaki Tsuchiya, vd vid företaget Tisco som äger en stor mängd av spelmaskinerna. En av dem som nu tillbringat ett par timmar vid en sådan maskin är Chiaki Sugai. Nu har hon fyllt en kundvagn med varor som kostat henne 8 000 yen. Förut köpte jag en massa godis i närbutiker, nu tar jag dem här i stället, säger hon.

articles.title: Sveriges framtida skydd – marina drönare
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Sveriges framtida skydd – marina drönare
articles.body_text: De marina drönarna väger omkring 900 kilo och är 4 meter långa. Sveriges framtida skydd – marina drönare Allting började i ett garage och med ett par vattenskotrar. I framtiden skulle det kunna vara försvarsbolaget Nautriks obemannade havsdrönare som patrullerar i Hormuzsundet eller skyddar Sveriges kustremsa. På avstånd smälter den nästan helt in i horisonten. Skillnaden blir omedelbar när den fyra meter långa och 850 kilo tunga farkosten får fart och forsar fram i vattnet utanför Lidingö i Stockholm. För dem som befinner sig till sjöss i området är det inte helt klart vad de faktiskt har sett passera i drygt 20 knop. Svaret är en ny typ av obemannad autonom drönare från det svenska försvarsbolaget Nautrik, tänkt att för både militärt och civilt bruk. Bakom företaget står grundaren och vd:n Oscar Fors, det var också i hans garage det hela startade. I och med Ukrainakriget gjorde jag som många andra och anmälde mig till Hemvärnet, men tänkte samtidigt att jag måste kunna göra något mer, säger han ombord på den stridsbåt där det går att följa och styra drönarna. Oscar Fors är vd för Nautrik, han har tidigare arbetat inom Northvolt och i Silicon Valley. Farkosten som Nautrik lanserat, Riverine 4, kan enkelt beskrivas som en helt obemannad drönare där systemet drivs av artificiell intelligens. Den här förmiddagen är det två båtar som ligger ute men avsikten är att en hel grupp ska kunna släppas ned från fartyg eller från land och operera i en enhetlig grupp. På en digital skärm visar en medarbetare i företaget en simulering av två marina drönare som får uppdraget att undersöka ett område till havs. Det ser ut som ett avancerat datorspel när de båda rör sig över skärmen och liknelsen är inte helt främmande. Vi har hämtat väldigt mycket från dataspelsvärlden hur man kan interagera och fått hjälp av några dataspelsgurus som startat stora bolag i Stockholm och blivit väldigt framgångsrika, säger Oscar Fors. På en medföljande båt går det att följa de marina drönarna. Här kan man också lägga upp olika uppdrag som till exempel en övervakning av ett specifikt område.

articles.title: Dyr bensin gör att amerikaner stannar hemma
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Dyr bensin gör att amerikaner stannar hemma
articles.body_text: Filmmakaren Josh Gaudette har tankat sin bil på en mack i den lilla staden Harrison i Michigan. Dyr bensin gör att amerikaner stannar hemma De skenande bränslepriserna är en av frågorna som bedöms kunna avgöra mellanårsvalet i USA. Det suger, säger dokumentärfilmaren Josh Gaudette från Michigan om bensinkostnaderna. Gaudette står på en mack i duggregnet i den lilla staden Harrison. Tidigare hade han en pickup. Nu har han bytt till en bränslesnål mindre bil. I Michigan ligger bensinpriset på över 4,60 dollar för en gallon (motsvarande 46 kronor för 3,78 liter). Historiskt har ett bensinpris på över 4 dollar per gallon ansetts vara ekonomiskt smärtsamt. Förra veckan skapade bränsleanalytikern Patrick De Haan stora rubriker när han konstaterade att USA under 2026 haft fler dagar med ett genomsnittligt pris på över 4 dollar än något år tidigare: nämligen 158. Innan president Donald Trump fattade beslut om att attackera Iran låg det genomsnittliga bensinpriset i USA på under 3 dollar per gallon. Nu är det 4,33 dollar, enligt motororganisationen AAA . Priset gör att jag isolerar mig. Jag struntar i att åka in till stan (Detroit) för det kostar 20 dollar i bensin. När jag var yngre älskade jag att köra omkring och upptäcka – det gör jag inte nu, berättar Gaudette. Pensionären Debbie, som inte vill uppge sitt efternamn, tankar vid pumpen intill. Hon har ett ord för bensinpriset: Debbie minns att priset per gallon legat runt 4 dollar tidigare. Men att det nu närmar sig 5 dollar är inget hon varit med om. Det gör att jag stannar hemma mer. Min dotter bor 45 minuter bort, förut hälsade jag på henne ofta. Nu gör jag inte det eftersom det kostar 30 dollar enkel väg bara i bensin.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.body_text: Publicerades: Mån 19 okt 02:00 Mån 19 okt • 6 min Moderaterna växer i alla landsbygdskommuner. Varför det? Aktuellt söker svaren till högersvängen i värmländska Sunne. Reportageserie om valets vinnare och förlorare. Mer om programmet Publicerades: Mån 12 okt 02:00 Mån 12 okt • 3 min 42 sek Succé i riksdagsvalet men flopp lokalt. Liberalerna backar i 215 av landets 290 kommuner. I 39 kommuner åker de ut helt. Aktuellt åkte till Botkyrka och Ekerö och sökte svar på det lokala misslyckandet. Mer om programmet Publiceras: Tor 29 okt 02:00 Tor 29 okt 02:00 • 8 min För första gången backade Sverigedemokraterna i ett riksdagsval. articles.title: Kulturnyheterna special: Avgörs valet på TikTok?
articles.summary: För första gången finns alla partiledare på Tiktok, samtidigt som nästan hälften av alla förstagångsväljare säger att de oftare tar del av politik på sociala medier än i tidningar, radio och tv. Vad gör det här med politiken, och är det på en kinesisk plattform som framställs som en säkerhetsrisk som det svenska valet kommer att avgöras? Medverkande: Emanuel Karlsten, journalist, Kajsa Falasca, forskare, och Oscar Samuelsson, kommunikationsrådgivare. Programledare: Cecilia Tiberg.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.summary: Arne Bivrins stora passion är fågelfotografi. Han kliver in i en sagovärld och tar bilder som får folk att häpna, av ögonblick som bara existerar där och då. articles.title: Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
articles.summary: After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming, writes Lucy Williamson.
articles.body_text: After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming. The general election on Tuesday hangs over a country that's deeply divided and ready for a fight. Polls published on Friday put the governing coalition and the main opposition bloc almost neck-and-neck, with half a million first-time voters due to cast their ballot and some 70,000 Israelis reportedly flying in from abroad specifically to vote. On Saturday night, vast crowds of opposition voters gathered in central Tel Aviv to demand a change of government. "We're optimistic," 21-year-old Omri told me. "I want peace, I want security, and I want to end corruption and get the religious fanatics out." This campaign has been energized by new tactics - including AI videos designed to grab the headlines - and also by a new face. Gadi Eisenkot is, perhaps, not the man you might expect to take on the flashy, aggressive, media-savvy brand of Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. Relatively new to politics, with a working-class Moroccan background, Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who is renowned for his calm manner and low-drama approach. He's been dubbed by some as a "non-politician". But he and his centrist Yashar party have regularly pipped Netanyahu and his Likud party to the top spot in recent polls, the last of which was published on Friday, in line with Israeli election law. Israeli politics is the art of coalition-building, rather than the task of any one party winning power, but with the predicted result too close to call, Eisenkot's rising profile has sharpened a race many Israelis already see as existential for the future of their country. I watched him slip past the cameras at a community centre for Ethiopian Jews in the city of Ramle last week, through a gaggle of security personnel and advisors. One of those who had come to hear him speak was David, a smartly dressed man in a freshly-pressed shirt and navy jacket, who said he had met Eisenkot before.

articles.title: Why Israel's election is one of the most important in its history
articles.summary: Security and democracy emerge as central issues in Israel's highly anticipated general election, as Middle East correspondent Lucy Williamson reports.
articles.body_text: Israeli voters are preparing to head to the polls in an election some have described as the most consequential in the country's history. It's the first general election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023. Tuesday's vote could see Benjamin Netanyahu's almost two-decade-long period of right-wing rule replaced by a more left-leaning government. Emerging as Netanyahu's main challenger is Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, who says the election is about Israel's identity as a liberal and tolerant democracy. Netanyahu has made security central to his campaign, warning that electing his rivals would risk making Israel less safe. Middle East correspondent Lucy Williamson reports. Dozens of people had been inside the church for a funeral when the shooting began, local media report. Orla Guerin travelled through Yemen, with forces loyal to its internationally recognised government, to a remote desert battlefield where Houthi rebels were dislodged just days ago. Security correspondent Frank Gardner explains how the Iran-backed Houthis' precision strikes and guerrilla tactics have made it difficult for Saudi forces to gain the upper hand. Footage from inside the airport shows the moment the strike hit on Saturday. The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for the remaining hostages held in Gaza. The BBC reports from a school in Taiz, Yemen, where children are determined to keep learning despite the vicious civil war. Witnesses say Raseel's tent was hit by an Israeli helicopter strike. articles.title: Serbia's veteran ruler Vučić concedes election to student-led protest movement
articles.summary: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.
articles.body_text: Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. "We still do not have final results... it is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded late on Sunday. Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement. Vučić had called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the 2024 collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence in Serbia. Vučić had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his party with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017. He made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade. There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle." The Student List - which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics - had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia. It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities. "This will be a free state," its lead candidate - cardiologist Ilija Srdanović - said in a statement to BBC Serbian as the result became clear. He said the movement hoped to "free the country from tyranny". The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control.

articles.title: Opposition leader María Machado returns to Venezuela
articles.summary: Machado had left the country just a month before the US government seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
articles.body_text: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. "I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil." "Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" González said. He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country "toward freedom". An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied. It's unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she's back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted. A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election - held outside the Maduro government's official election authority - in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote. Despite winning the primary, Maduro's government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize.

articles.title: Suspect in deadly Paris suburb shooting sent for psychiatric observation
articles.summary: He will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation", authorities said.
articles.body_text: A man suspected of a deadly gun attack near Paris has left custody and been placed under psychiatric observation, French anti-terrorism officials have said. One person was killed and five others injured on Friday when an attacker opened fire from his car - first in Trappes, and then in nearby La Verrière - appearing to target people of migrant origin. The suspect, named in French media as 39-year-old Kevin T, will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation", the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said. President Emmanuel Macron called it a "racist terrorist attack", adding that people had been targeted over their skin colour or religion. It marked a "turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation", the French president said. PNAT said the move to place the suspect under psychiatric evaluation followed guidance from a psychiatric expert. The evaluation will determine whether the suspect should remain in police custody and is "likely to last 48 hours", PNAT added. PNAT said the suspect was also found to have cannabis and cocaine in his bloodstream. French newspaper Le Monde and news agency AFP report that a Bible, a Quran and a copy of Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf were found at the suspect's home, citing a source close to the investigation. The lawyer for Pengo Bossio Wangi, the one person killed during the attack, told French media the move to place the suspect under observation was "very rare". He alleged that it was being used to portray the suspect as criminally irresponsible rather than having acted deliberately. Wangi, a 26-year-old French-Congolese martial artist, was named as the one fatality on Saturday.

articles.title: Gabon says access to social media restored after eight-month ban
articles.summary: The authorities had justified the ban by saying online content was fuelling conflict, while the opposition had condemned it as an abuse of power.
articles.body_text: Gabon says it has lifted a ban on social media imposed eight months ago - a move that triggered widespread criticism at the time. The High Communication Authority (HAC) announced the U-turn on Saturday in a televised statement. The BBC has approached the country's media regulator for comment. The ban had been introduced on 17 February, with the HAC saying that online content was fuelling conflict and deepening divisions in the country. The move came as a shock to the central African nation of about 2.5 million people, where social media platforms such as Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram have been particularly popular with younger people who use it for business as well as pleasure. Many turned to VPNs in order to continue accessing social media sites following the ban. The ban had been imposed at a time when the Gabonese President Brice Oligui Nguema was facing a wave of social unrest less than a year after his election. Teachers and civil servants had staged strikes over what they said were low pay and poor working conditions. The opposition said the suspension was an abuse of power. Nguema won last year's elections with more than 90% of the vote, two years after his coup had ended more than five decades of rule by the Bongo family. At the time he pledged to reform Gabon, a small, oil- and timber-rich country, where digital blackouts were used by the previous governments to control information.

articles.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
articles.summary: Nayib Bukele says bodies delivered to soldiers are "not our men" amid search for Salvadorans abducted last week.
articles.body_text: Four bodies handed over to special forces on a mission to Haiti to recover Salvadoran hostages are "not our men", El Salvador's president has said. Nayib Bukele said a nongovernmental organisation delivered the human remains to one of Haiti's airports claiming they were four El Salvadoran air technicians, but that one of the corpses was a child's and another was wearing a different country's army uniform. He had dispatched a military contingent, reportedly of hundreds of soldiers, on Thursday after the four men vanished after being ambushed by "heavily armed criminal groups". The hostages had been part of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), which is tasked with tackling worsening gang violence in Haiti. The men had been travelling back to their camp in an armoured vehicle when they were attacked in an area of the Caribbean island nation controlled by armed groups called Croix-des-Bouquets. No gang has so far claimed responsibility. Bukele previously said the Salvadoran military operation in Haiti had the sole purpose of returning the four men alive. Approximately 450 soldiers had so far been deployed, according to Haitian newspaper Le Nouvelliste. Bukele said the bodies the mission had received included one of a man of "considerably greater height than that of our air technicians", a person "who was wearing part of a uniform from an army that is not ours", and that among the remains were identification cards and uniforms from other countries. He posted pictures showing the ID card of a GSF member and a corresponding national ID card from Chad in Africa. Bukele's comments poured skepticism on an earlier report in the New York Times, citing people close to the Salvadoran mission, that the bodies found on the outskirts of the Haitian capital, Port-au-Prince, on Saturday were thought to belong to the missing men. The newspaper reported that the bodies delivered to the military contingent had been badly burned, meaning a medical examination would be required to identify them. It cited one unnamed source briefed on the situation as saying the ID posted by Bukele in fact belonged to a soldier who had lost it when he had been injured. Haiti has been ravaged by gang violence for years, but the situation has worsened in the political vacuum that followed the assassination of its president in 2021.

articles.title: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
articles.summary: The tech billionaire accuses Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using the network for military activity.
articles.body_text: Elon Musk has said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved. The tech billionaire accused Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using it for military activity - but denied being responsible for a simultaneous issue with its US-run, military-grade counterpart Starshield. Kyiv has not officially commented on Musk's latest claim but Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said his post was "very strange". Musk had earlier denied deliberately throttling Ukraine's connection, which it says hampered its ability to conduct defensive operations for more than a week. The issue first emerged last week during a broader row between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Musk's latest comments, and the seeming restoration of the service, came after US President Donald Trump said he had told the Tesla and X owner to "put it back", having repeatedly denied instructing him to limit the service. "Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote on X on Saturday. "Ukraine['s] military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week." He went on to say that SpaceX had "done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth" and reiterated his stipulation that Starshield was a different system and controlled by the US government, adding: "What they decide to do is up to them." He added in a later post: "[Starlink] can be used for infrastructure that is military, but it cannot be used for unequivocally offensive strikes that make it fair game to be struck back." Reacting to Musk's post, Beskrestnov said that drones operating via Starlink in Ukraine had a speed restriction of 70-90km/h (43-56mph) and did not work on Russian territory. "Therefore, we physically cannot use commercial Starlink for deep strikes and medium-range strikes," he wrote on Telegram.

articles.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
articles.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announces restrictions on the movement of Palestinian workers in the run-up to Tuesday's election.
articles.body_text: All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements. The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory. The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday. It said most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas. Before the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major operation on Friday in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed. The Israeli military have been demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron, with hundreds of families having been displaced . Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which has led to at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened, according to footage shared online. Even before the entry and exit bans on workers were announced by the IDF on Sunday, the military had cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents. It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis in the West Bank - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment. Friday's shooting came during a tense time for the region, just days ahead of Israel's election taking place on Tuesday. In an interview with Israel's i24 television channel released on Saturday, Netanyahu threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority (PA), which governs parts of the territory.

articles.title: Death toll in Nigeria village raided by gunmen rises to 48, police say
articles.summary: Unidentified gunmen on motorcycles swooped on a remote village on Friday, looting shops and setting houses ablaze.
articles.body_text: The death toll from Friday's attack on a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba has risen to at least 48, police have told the BBC. The police had initially reported 10 deaths after unidentified gunmen on motorcycles raided the village of Binnari, looting shops and setting houses ablaze. More bodies were discovered on Sunday, according to state police spokesperson Victor Mshelizah, who said some of the victims had drowned while trying to escape the attackers while others were killed in nearby bushes. Meanwhile, Amnesty International's director for Nigeria said his organisation had confirmed 52 deaths, citing sources on the ground and members of the local community. The attack happened just after midday Muslim prayers, and the rampage went on for up to four hours. State police had initially recovered 10 bodies with gunshot wounds after officers responded to a distress call. The attackers had fled by the time officers arrived - but they continued to patrol the area to restore calm, Taraba's police told the BBC on Saturday. "We were able to disperse the unknown gunmen though there was no casualty on their side and ours because the terrain is difficult and they're used to the terrain," Assistant Superintendent of Police Victor Mshelizah said. Community leader Malam Abubakar Saifullahi told news agency AFP that the attackers had arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece. "They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions," he said. "They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack." Isiyaku Musa, who survived the attack, told AFP: "People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go." Amnesty's Nigeria director Isa Sanusi has called for an impartial investigation into the killings, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity".

articles.summary: Voters in Sunday's election are choosing between two very different candidates, as Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body_text: Polls have opened in Brazil to vote for the country's next president. Brazilians are choosing between Brazil's current left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro, the son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, beat Lula in the first round of voting on 4 October by a narrow margin. articles.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: Obama said the election was "the last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration".
articles.body_text: Former US President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections. "This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration's immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters "we're in the golden age of America". The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans. Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump. Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members while speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, at one point mocking the president's attempt to redecorate the White House. "After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'enough is enough'," the former president said in Cleveland. Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy. "If you thought everything was too expensive before 'you know who'," he said, referring to Trump without using his name, "everything is more expensive now". Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were "temporarily high" but said "our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down". The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry "we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs" and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress.

articles.title: Fireworks and tear gas as protesters and riot police clash in Paris
articles.summary: The BBC's Europe correspondent reports from Paris where mostly peaceful protests turned into unrest after nightfall.
articles.body_text: Police have clashed with protesters in Paris as some demonstrations in France turned violent on Saturday. A largely peaceful day of protests turned into unrest after nightfall, as protesters were seen throwing objects and fireworks at police. Around 70,000 officers were deployed across France for a second consecutive weekend and used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. The Interior Ministry estimated around 400,000 people took part in Saturday's demonstrations, with nearly 1,000 arrests made. Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Paris, where he says there are few signs the unrest will ease soon. Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man following the fire. The three waves of Russian missiles were launched at hours after Russia said it was "ready in principle" to resume peace talks with the US and Ukraine. articles.title: More than 1,300 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations in France, with protests also taking place in other European countries.
articles.body_text: More than 1,300 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France on Saturday that were followed by some clashes later in the day, officials have said. After largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. Officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history. The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000. Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched. The interior ministry said 53 officers were hurt in clashes across the country on Saturday. French President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings. Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city's Porte d'Italie towards Porte de Vincennes, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism. Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership. French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters", news agency AFP reported. The Interior Ministry said 142 people were arrested in the French capital on Saturday, less than half of the number arrested on the same day last week. In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city.

articles.title: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?
articles.summary: Conoce el calendario oficial de feriados en Perú para 2026 y revisa qué días libres quedan en los últimos meses del año. Consulta las fechas de noviembre y diciembre para planificar tus viajes, actividades familiares o próximos descansos.
articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?
articles.summary: Conoce el calendario oficial de feriados en Perú para 2026 y revisa qué días libres quedan en los últimos meses del año. Consulta las fechas de noviembre y diciembre para planificar tus viajes, actividades familiares o próximos descansos.
articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated ‘Odyssey’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The footage looks okay, as long as you're not seeking artistry, inspiration, or human interest.
articles.body_text: Three months after Elon Musk declared that Grok would release a full-length, “historically accurate” movie version of “The Odyssey,” Grok has published a whole seven minutes — what the company is now calling “Episode 1 of our Odyssey series.” Musk had previously lashed out at Christopher Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” because Nolan cast nonwhite and transgender actors. And Nolan is, in many ways, a perfect foil for Musk — while SpaceX and Tesla CEO hypes up data centers in space and posts an unending stream of AI-generated content, Nolan has described himself as “a techno-skeptic ” and said that before AI, he’d never seen a technology “so completely rejected by the public.” And while Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” certainly used plenty of visual effects, it’s primarily a feat of practical filmmaking , with a shoot spanning six countries and a cast and crew of thousands. After its release in July, the film became an extraordinary box office success , selling out Imax screenings for months and becoming the likely front-runner at the next Academy Awards . As for the Grok version of “The Odyssey” (created in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker), well, you can watch for yourself. Watch Episode 1 of our Odyssey series made with Grok Imagine. Let us know in the comments if you'd like a full breakdown of how it was done! Creative collaboration with @WonderStudiosX and director Dev Walker @glumlot_ pic.twitter.com/xpgpkqSCpq I’ll admit it’s not as spectacularly ugly as I’d expected, and certainly more impressive than other videos that Musk has posted recently. If I didn’t know better, there were moments when I might have thought these were real actors sailing across a real sea. And while I can’t speak to Grok’s historical accuracy, it does seem that all the characters come in a Musk-approved skin color, while the narrator uses a British accent that will sound familiar to anyone who’s played a fantasy video game or watched a generic Hollywood epic from the past 25 years. What the footage really lacks is any sense of artistry, inspiration, or human interest. The backstory — delivered via the aforementioned voiceover — seems to go on forever, finally giving way to one bearded face after another, each shouting stilted lines that make Nolan’s dialogue sound like Shakespeare. While a few individual shots might provide a reasonable simulacrum of reality, the whole thing feels completely airless, offering viewers no sense of momentum, no reason to care about anyone or anything on-screen. And where I had no trouble paying attention for the nearly three-hour runtime of Nolan’s “Odyssey,” I was listlessly checking how much I had left before the Grok version was even halfway through. It’s hard to imagine being interested in another seven minutes of this, much less a full movie’s worth. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: ‘Cyberselfish’ author takes aim at techno-libertarianism as her book returns from the dead | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "That's a 12-year-old view of the world."
articles.body_text: It’s hard for books about technology to age well. They always risk becoming outdated as companies rise and fall, and as one hot new product is replaced by the next. But last year, “Nerd Reich” author Gil Durán declared that it was time to revive the career of Paulina Borsook, who he said “saw it all very clearly and tried to warn us 25 years ago.” Later that fall, The New York Times reported that Borsook’s “Cyberselfish ” — first published in 2000 — was finding new fans who want to understand why the tech industry “lost its way.” Now, long after going out of print, “Cyberselfish” is returning in a new edition from Tin House . Borsook told me in a Zoom interview that the book is meant to be “almost a travelogue” of her attempts to understand what she calls the techno-libertarian influence on Silicon Valley culture. “That’s a 12-year-old view of the world,” Borsook said, describing it as “a kind of basket of beliefs” that’s “violently anti-regulation,” despite the fact that “no sector of society had benefited more and suffered less from the government than these guys.” In her telling, “even after the dot-com crash, that attitude was just there, percolating around, contaminating the aquifers. It was uncorrected, and it just spread out more and more.” Borsook has yet to publish a second book, and she said that after “Cyberselfish” was first released, “no one was interested in anything I might have to say about anything, tech or not tech, forever after.” But last year, she began to notice that prices for used copies were beginning to creep up, and she was starting to see “very out-of-the-blue, I-did-not-know-these-people posts on social media about how important this book was,” as well as inquiries from “European academics,” eventually leading to more press coverage and the new Tin House edition, with a new introduction by Durán. Keep reading for our full conversation, edited for length and clarity, in which Borsook discusses AI, how Silicon Valley has transformed in the past 25 years, and what advice she has for young people seeking a career in tech. Do you want to talk a little bit about how your interest in techno-libertarianism started, and how you decided that there was a book in this? Everything with me is always inadvertent. I started knocking around tech circles, however we define it, in the early-middle ‘80s, in the Bay Area. And then I would say, starting around maybe the early ‘90s, I would hear these — to me — very weird, offhand remarks that some people would make that I couldn’t make any sense out of. It’s not my nature to argue with people. It’s my nature to listen, and so I didn’t have the term for it except libertarian. But it seemed very screwy because initially, I grew up in Pasadena, which was [the home of the] Caltech-JPL space program, and so the parents of the kids I knew were another STEM culture. When I first got into Silicon Valley, I thought, “Oh, this is just another STEM culture like I’m familiar with.” And those guys [at Caltech and JPL] had a very clear sense of what the government can do for you, were not into enlightened self-interest. It was a different personality type, and they certainly didn’t self-anoint with how glorious and grand and magisterial they were, even though they were doing great things. I was just listening, I guess, and being confused. Even then, I knew no sector of society had benefited more and suffered less from the government than these guys. So why are they acting like this?

articles.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech."
articles.body_text: AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said. Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.” “AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment,” he wrote, later adding, “AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness, all of which shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.” Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains . articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Blue-green is the color of autonomy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
articles.body_text: U.S. federal safety regulators continue to tackle the sticky problem of autonomous vehicles, this time with a proposal that could signal to the public, quite literally, when a vehicle is operating autonomously. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has proposed new lighting requirements for autonomous vehicles that include an option (dare I say a strong suggestion?) to use cyan-colored lights to signal when a vehicle is operating autonomously without a human occupant monitoring the road. The agency is not proposing a mandate for blue-green lights. Importantly, under the proposal, the lights would be used when an AV is operating in autonomous mode. Still, federal regulators are clearly seeking some uniform way of identifying autonomous vehicles. The proposal establishes equipment specifications, including where the lights are mounted, the color they emit, and how they’re activated. It would also remove requirements for manually operated controls for turn signals, high beams, and hazard lights. Under the proposal, the NHTSA suggests the lights be cyan (blue-green), remain steadily illuminated rather than flash, and be visible from the front, rear, and both sides. This latest proposal is one piece of a bigger effort to update regulations that help speed up the adoption of AVs while maintaining safety, according to NHTSA administrator Jonathan Morrison. The agency is already working on a federal automated vehicle framework and is trying to update federal motor vehicle safety standards, which already govern automakers today. For instance, FMVSS rules were not designed for vehicles like the Tesla Cybercab and Zoox robotaxi, which lack traditional, federally required equipment like pedals, steering wheels, and design features like side mirrors and rearview mirrors. While the feds wrestle over regulating the future of transportation, GM laid out how it plans to be part of it. The automaker held its annual GM Forward event, and a lot of what was announced builds on last year’s push into AI. But now we have more details and dates. The U.S. automaker is overhauling the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant that will change its 30-year-old OnStar service. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also roll out an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over. GM has also adopted enterprise AI across the company to slash its traditional four- to five-year development timeline in half.

articles.title: The hottest AI wearables and gadgets you should know about | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We compiled a list of all the hottest AI wearables, including Muse Charm, Bee, Friend, Plaud, and more.
articles.body_text: A slew of AI-powered gadgets on the market aims to integrate artificial intelligence into our daily lives like never before. Some of these AI wearables — including necklaces, rings, and wristbands, as well as portable devices — serve as productivity tools, while others claim to act as friendly companions listening to your everyday thoughts. Even OpenAI is working on a compact AI companion device. Below, we’ve rounded up some of the most notable devices. The companion app (currently available only on iOS) is included with a $19 monthly subscription. The app allows you to interact with Bee directly and ask it questions. You can also get key takeaways from your day and chronological transcripts of your conversations. Amazon acquired the wearables startup in July 2025, launching its first new products earlier this month. Amazon introduced two new devices: the Bee Frontier, priced at $74.99, which can be worn on the wrist or clipped to clothing, and the Bee Eclipse, priced at $99.99, a credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of a smartphone. Both offer the same core functionality as the previous generation, positioning Bee as a more affordable alternative to AI devices such as the Plaud Note and Plaud NotePin. Users can also choose to connect Bee to Alexa. Friend is one of the most hyped entrants in the “personal AI” device market. This $129 white pendant hangs around your neck and functions as an emotional support companion. It recognizes your tone and mood, allowing you to chat with it as if it were a friend. It connects to your phone via Bluetooth and constantly listens, ready to respond or send you proactive messages, like wishing you good luck before an interview. However, it has also faced criticism, including backlash against its subway ad campaign in NYC. People vandalized the ads, writing messages like “surveillance capitalism.” Likely as an attempt to stay relevant, the company recently unveiled a major product update, introducing a new voice feature. Under the name “Friend 2.0,” the updated device includes a built-in speaker that allows it to communicate with users and express a more distinctive personality. Formerly known as Rewind, Limitless is another conversation-recording pendant priced at $99.

articles.title: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Elon Musk reportedly ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine's Starlink access.
articles.body_text: SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions the Ukrainian military’s of use Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system. The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions. This follows a 10-day period where Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly. President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, with Musk recently posting , “Zelensky has gone too far.” The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.” “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.” Buy One Pass, Get a Second Free Cover more ground at TechCrunch’s ultimate founder bootcamp of the year by bringing your co-founder or partner for free Book before the BOGO deal expires Every weekday and Sunday, you can get the best of TechCrunch’s coverage.
