articles.title: Will AI expose the rickety infrastructure of the internet? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The moment you realize the internet is "held together by glue and dreams."
articles.body_text: A startling announcement went out earlier this week: Due to recently discovered vulnerabilities in the open source programming language PHP, website owners had to immediately patch their sites — or if they couldn’t update right away, they should take the sites down to be safe. On this week’s episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the significance of the PHP-ocalypse and whether we’ll see more incidents like this in the future. Sean called this “a real reckoning moment” that highlights how “when you get down to the bone level of the internet,” everything seems to be “held together by glue and dreams.” And with widespread access to large language models and AI agents, it’s only going to become easier to find these vulnerabilities. (That said, these specific vulnerabilities were found by human researchers , not AI models.) Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Sean O’Kane: The internet is breaking in lots of ways this week, it seems. I think the best way to think about this, if people are coming into this kind of cold: How many times over the last 10 years have we had these moments where something breaks or something nearly breaks, where one person maintaining one tiny repro repository as a hobby or whatever happens to catch that something nefarious is going on and and saves us from the infrastructure of the internet completely crumbling? Now multiply that by a billion, when people have access to not only extremely advanced software in the form of these LLMs that everybody uses, but also the ability to task them to go out and do it themselves, with creating AI agents that are single-minded at accomplishing those things. We’re seeing a balance of two things happening this week. One is a bunch of the labs and companies like Google and OpenAI actually had people go out and find a bunch of vulnerabilities, including the one with PHP. And then we also have a bunch of people seeming to rush to take advantage of those vulnerabilities to try and hack into websites. So we have governments taking down websites, we have really popular websites that are going down briefly to be able to fix this vulnerability. This is a real reckoning moment, where we’re going to find out the downside risk of building so much of the internet on open source technology like PHP. When you really get down to the bone level of the internet, it is held together with glue and dreams. Anthony Ha: There’s so many things that were striking about this. One of them is the fact that — as I understand it, at least — this is not a new vulnerability. This is a vulnerability that has existed in PHP for decades. And PHP has been used as a programming language to build so much of the web, so this vulnerability has been there for decades, but no one knew about it. What happened is, essentially, that these big AI companies — including Wiz, now owned by Google — they were able to find these vulnerabilities using LLMs. [As noted above, I got this wrong: Human researchers participating in OpenAI and Wiz’s Hack the Planet initiative found the vulnerabilities , though they used AI to exploit the bug.] I guess part of the calculation is, we need to patch this, because if we can find this vulnerability using LLMs, so can other people. But the only way we can get the patch out there is to announce the vulnerability. And so it creates this very panicked situation where [they say]: “Okay, this vulnerability existed for decades. You have to patch right away, and if you can’t patch it right away, just take your website down. It’s that severe a vulnerability.”

articles.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn't make it | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
articles.body_text: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry. Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate “Chat,” “Codex,” and “Work” modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version “ChatGPT Classic.” The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after , bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back. That wasn’t OpenAI’s only attempt to pull everything under one roof. The company has also shut down several stand-alone apps and folded their features directly into ChatGPT — a strategy that’s worked out better than the redesign did. ChatGPT Atlas, a stand-alone AI-powered web browser, lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT. The company did the same thing with Operator , an AI agent that could browse the web and complete tasks on a user’s behalf, and OpenAI has increasingly built image generation directly into ChatGPT, shrinking the role of DALL-E as its own separate destination for creating images. We also can’t forget its video-sharing platform, Sora , which struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026. When Apple unveiled Apple Intelligence in 2024, an improved Siri was one of the highlighted features. The pitch promised a Siri that could understand context, know what was happening across apps, and get tasks done effectively. However, Apple repeatedly pushed back the release of the new Siri, citing various reasons like engineering issues and bugs . This delay eventually contributed to a $250 million settlement over claims regarding how Apple marketed the AI capabilities of the iPhone 16. Siri AI finally appeared in the iOS 27 beta this past July, with the new AI-powered version rolling out to English-language users first this month; support for other languages is expected to follow.

articles.title: Block's new voice model sounds eerily human | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Block said that the voice model can run locally on a MacBook M4 Max
articles.body_text: Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model out of the company’s research lab that runs locally and sounds strangely human with its expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model, called Dessa, is trained fully on human speech and a single NVIDIA GPU rack. Dessa is a full-duplex model, which means it can talk and listen at the same time, just like the GPT-Live model OpenAI released earlier this year . Typically, speech models are paired with a large language model for knowledge retrieval. Block said that Dessa’s knowledge stems from the conversational data it has. We believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence. https://t.co/r0qFLdvd6c Block said that the current models can sound unnatural and annoying because they have text in the pipeline that drives speech generation. A lot of models like ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio Drama 3 use voice tags to drive emotion in speech generation. Dorsey’s company claims that emotion is built into its model. It’s not clear if that emotion is being steered by some kind of tags. “Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous,” the company said in a blog post . The company’s researchers posted multiple examples of conversations with Dessa where the agent had different voices, cadences, and emotions. For instance, in the conversation, the bot said it was tired from work, and at that point it sounded tired. We made the first AI model you can have a realistic conversation with that was trained entirely on speech! Dessa is a full-duplex speech-to-speech model that you can run on consumer GPUs. This is a GPT3 moment for speech. pic.twitter.com/XVD8sSyJn8 In the example below, the bot was talking about the person making it comfortable while sounding emotional and almost breaking down. Dessa=full-duplex speech model vs Human=me, https://t.co/1eI6QFHo1w pic.twitter.com/zlZfxH2BA5 Another one shows a Block team member playing a game with the voice assistant. For the love of the game. Watch Cara play a guessing game with Dessa. The model guesses the first one right straight away, and the second doesn’t take long either. https://t.co/FDmoXNPpIh pic.twitter.com/I9f8saduEA The company said that the model can run locally on a consumer-grade computer such as a MacBook M4 Max or better. However, there is no public access to Dessa at the moment, and Block has put out a call for safety researchers to test the model. This is likely to test out cases where a voice agent could trick people on the other end.

articles.title: PHP-ocalypse: How two critical web bugs almost broke the internet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Two critical bugs in the PHP web programming language, used by the majority of the internet, threatened to upend the internet — and it's unlikely to be the last major software scare.
articles.body_text: On Wednesday, a decades-old open-source web technology called PHP almost broke the internet, thanks to two vulnerabilities that had sat dormant for years until researchers recently figured out a way to exploit them. The bugs are dubbed PHP2Shell , officially designated as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . In simple terms, the bugs allow anyone who knows how to exploit them to break into an online system running PHP, such as a website or internet-facing server, without needing a password to access or modify its data. As situations go, this was a pretty sizable one, forcing millions of people around the world to scramble to patch their systems before malicious hackers could abuse them. The PHP Foundation, which maintains the PHP web software, publicly released patches on Wednesday that fixed the bugs, which when installed prevent web-facing servers from being attacked. The foundation had already given some of the biggest internet companies and web hosts that rely on PHP an early headstart on patching. Thanks to weeks of backroom chatter and careful coordination across the industry, the world — so far — broadly avoided mass internet exploitation. From Wednesday, governments began urging citizens and companies with websites to take action to mitigate the risks on their ends. A wide range of industries shuttered their websites and pulled services offline to patch their systems. Banks, retailers, gaming sites, online stores, hospitals, and some government agencies took down their servers to prevent attacks. But security researchers are warning that the situation isn’t over yet, and that a large number of systems around the world remain unpatched and vulnerable to hacks and data theft. This is also unlikely to be the last major internet software scare, with some expecting the advent of AI to rapidly uncover as-yet-undiscovered vulnerabilities that are waiting to be found and abused. Security researchers at Calif found two bugs in PHP, a programming language widely used around the world for building websites and web apps, both on the internet and hosted locally on company networks, like intranets and internal sites. PHP is open-source, meaning it’s free and available to be used by anyone for almost any reason. As such, it’s become one of the most popular and broadly used web programming languages on the web today. The two bugs were first discovered in 2024 but weren’t considered exploitable at the time, and weren’t patched. Security researchers recently found a way to exploit them, prompting them to alert the makers of the software to get them fixed. Calif alerted the PHP Foundation, which began a period of fixing the bugs and coordinated disclosure. The foundation did this by offering the information and patches about the security issues under a tightly guarded embargo — essentially held confidentially until a specific deadline — to give big companies an opportunity to get ahead of installing the fixes. PHP2Shell is pretty serious because it can be abused remotely over the internet and without the victim having to click on a link or open a file. This is known as remote code execution , and it’s one of the more damaging kinds of bugs to exploit because they can grant a hacker anywhere in the world effectively full control over an affected and unpatched system.

articles.title: Unprotected license plate surveillance cameras let anyone with a web browser tune in
articles.summary: The Verge is about technology and how it makes us feel. Founded in 2011, we offer our audience everything from breaking news to reviews to award-winning features and investigations, on our site, in video, and in podcasts.
articles.body_text: Automated license plate recognition systems, also known as ALPR or simply LPR systems, have become increasingly popular — and controversial — tools for law enforcement in recent years. The systems can automatically photograph and record data on license plates in real time, drawing the ire of privacy advocates like those at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, which has just released information on security vulnerabilities in ALPR systems across the country. “Earlier this year, EFF learned that more than a hundred ALPR cameras were exposed online, often with totally open Web pages accessible by anyone with a browser,” the organization says in the new report released today. The report focuses on systems sold by a company called PIPS Technology, which is now owned by 3M. According to the EFF, live feeds from some of the cameras were available to watch online, and “were individually connected to the internet and freely accessible online to anyone who knew where to look.” The organization described its testing approach: The testing process involved confirming that a camera was online and responding to requests by connecting to it with a Web browser or by connecting to it over Telnet. If the camera had a password on both the Web and Telnet interface we left it alone, but if the camera was not protected with a password we were able to recover configuration information. However, when the Web was locked down, but Telnet was not, we [were] able to view password information in the Telnet configuration. Often these passwords were set to the default or were otherwise not sophisticated enough to be secure.Using information embedded on the page and through publicly available sources, the EFF was able to identify the position of some of the cameras, and got in touch with the owners to highlight the vulnerabilities. Some, like local Louisiana law enforcement agencies and the University of Southern California, took steps to fix the vulnerabilities. But the city of Hialeah, Florida, stopped returning the organization’s calls. The ACLU has found that about three-quarters of law enforcement agencies were using similar systems in 2011, giving officers “hundreds of millions of data points” on drivers not accused of a crime.

articles.title: Erkänner: ”Klart att vi har förlorat valet”
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic och hans nationalistiska regeringsparti SNS erkänner nederlag i söndagens extra parlamentsval i Serbien.
articles.body_text: Aleksandar Vucic och hans nationalistiska regeringsparti SNS erkänner nederlag i söndagens extra parlamentsval i Serbien. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. – Baserat på ett stratifierat urval står det klart att vi har förlorat valet, säger Vucic till anhängare vid partiets högkvarter i Belgrad sent på söndagskvällen. Han hänvisar alltså till statistik som bygger på olika variabler. De visar att den relativt nybildade – och i stort sett ledarlösa – oppositionsrörelsen Studentlistan gått starkare än SNS i valet, rapporterar nyhetsbyrån AFP. Därmed är 14 år av SNS-styre i landet över. Vucic lämnade för några veckor sedan presidentposten med sikte på att bli premiärminister vid en eventuell valseger. Vucic skyllde förlusten på Serbiens oberoende medier, på påstådd inblandning från icke namngivna europeiska länder och på USA:s ”djupa stat”, rapporterar AP. När Vucic erkänt sig besegrad utbröt firande på huvudstaden Belgrads gator. Förbipasserande bilar tutade, och folksamlingar började fira nära valmyndighetens högkvarter. Vid Studentlistans högkvarter grät och jublade anhängare. De kramade om varandra medan de ropade: Studenten Mila Martic befann sig vid högkvarteret: – Det känns helt otroligt. Det känns som om jag äntligen lever i ett fritt land, sade hon. Redan när köerna började ringla långa utanför vallokalerna i landet anade många att ett högt valdeltagande skulle gynna Studentlistan. Med två timmar kvar till att vallokalerna skulle stänga uppgav myndigheterna att nästan 65 procent av de röstberättigade hade röstat. Det kan jämföras med att det totala valdeltagandet 2023 var knappt 59 procent.

I kommentarsfältet är många upprörda över att en AI-genererad bild riktar sig mot barn. – Många har skrivit att den kan upplevas som obehaglig. Vissa saker såg nästan demoniska ut. Linnéa Söderström upplever att företag struntar i att det tydligt syns att saker gjorts med AI.

articles.summary: Valet i Brasilien ser ut att bli jämnt. I sista stund har båda presidentkandidaterna vänt sig till domstol – för att förlänga vallokalernas öppettider. Nu förlängs valet med två timmar.
articles.body_text: I sista stund har båda presidentkandidaterna vänt sig till domstol – för att förlänga vallokalernas öppettider. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I början av oktober hölls en första omgång i det brasilianska presidentvalet, som står mellan den sittande presidenten Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva och utmanaren Flávio Bolsonaro. Då fick ingen av dem över 50 procent av rösterna – och på söndagen hålls därför en ny omgång. Valet beskrivs som ovanligt jämnt, och enligt en ny opinionsundersökning har kandidaterna 50 procent vardera av väljarnas stöd. Vallokalerna skulle stänga klockan 21, svensk tid, men en dryg timme före det gick Lula da Silva ut med att han ville att öppettiderna skulle förlängas i bland annat Salvador och São Paulo. Detta efter att kollektivtrafiken i städerna ska ha störts , med bussar som tagits ut trafik, så att väljare inte kunnat ta sig fram till vallokalerna. – Vi vill ha ett ärligt val där alla har rätt att rösta, säger presidenten enligt BBC. Han ber också väljarna att ”inte ge upp”. – Vänta, och rösta, för demokrati måste vinna. Samtidigt har Bolsonaro bett om extra tid i flera städer i sammanlagt tre delstater på grund av dåligt väder, skriver Reuters. Listan verkar ha följts troget under det råa mordet på en 18-årig man i Fruängen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Ildar Galiyev har åtalats som misstänks bland annat för tre mord, ett fall av anstiftan av mord, ett mordförsök, och tre fall av anstiftan till mordförsök. I februari utlämnades han från Grekland. Därifrån misstänks han via krypterade chattar ha beställt och styrt Dalennätverkets mord och våldsdåd under kriget mot Rawa ”Kurdiske räven” Majids nätverk Foxtrot. Ett av de mer uppmärksammade dåden som han misstänks ha styrt gäller mordet på en 18-årig man, en rapartist, i Fruängen , den 27 september 2023. Tonåringen uppgavs ha haft kopplingar till Foxtrot. Drygt två veckor efter skjutmordet gjorde polisen en husrannsakan hos en 22-årig man i Järfälla. Han pekas ut som en så kallad ”möjliggörare” och vapenansvarig för Dalennätverket. Han hade haft tät kontakt på krypterade meddelandeappen Signal med alias som polisen kopplar till Galiyev. Husrannsakan utfördes efter att polisen stoppat en taxibil i Uppsala som 22-åringen satt i – och i bagageutrymmet hittat 25 kilo sprängmedel förpackat i dubbla Ikeapåsar. I 22-åringens bostad hittades två handskrivna, avrivna sidor med instruktioner om hur ett skjutmord ska förberedas, utföras och hur risken att gripas ska minimeras.

articles.title: Pastorn om Malexander-mördarens besök
articles.summary: Tony Byström, tidigare Olsson, dömdes till livstid för Malexandermorden 1999. I dag talade han i ”Life Church” på Södermalm i Stockholm om sina upplevelser.
articles.body_text: Tony Olsson, numera Byström, dömdes 1999 till livstid för polismorden i Malexander. På söndagen var han inbjuden att berättade sin historia under en gudstjänst i frikyrkan ”Life Church” i Stockholm. Något som mött kraftig kritik i sociala medier. – Vi kan inte göra analysen utifrån den intensiva kritiken som var på Facebook. Den är orimlig, säger pastorn Rune Borgsö. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Tony Olsson har bytt efternamn till Byström efter att ha suttit i fängelse för Malexandermorden 1999 och den uppmärksammade rymningen från Hallanstalten 2004. När frikyrkan Life Church på Södermalm i Stockholm meddelade att han skulle hålla en predikan under söndagsgudstjänsten rasade kommentarerna in. ”Varför ska Tony få dela sin berättelse när poliserna i Malexander inte får det?” , skrev en användare i kommentarsfältet. ”Vilket fullständigt vidrigt evenemang som ni sitter och vurmar för. Skäms”, skriver en annan. Inlägget fick över tusen kommentarer innan det togs bort, vilket Aftonbladet var först med att rapportera. Olsson blev inbjuden av kyrkans pastor, Rune Borgsö. Han har varit pastor och missionär i över 40 år på församlingen Livets Ord i Uppsala. De har känt varandra sedan Olsson kom ut ur fängelset 2023, då Olsson fick villkorlig dom efter att ha avtjänat två tredjedelar av sitt straff. Borgsö säger att de blev tagna på sängen av kritiken på sociala medier.
